pr_title: fix(core): Host classes should not be fed back into `@Input`
pr_body:
Previously all static styling information (including the ones from component/directive host bindings) would get merged into a single value before it would be written into the `@Input('class'/'style')`. The new behavior specifically excludes host values from the `@Input` bindings.

Fix #35383

issue_context.title: Input with name "class" and host binding for class have a different behaviour in ng8 and ng9
issue_context.body:
# 🐞 bug report

### Affected Package
The issue is caused by package @angular/core


### Is this a regression?
Yes, in angular before version 9 this bug was not presented.
Before ng9 @Input properties don't be affected with host.class.


### Description

```
@Component({
  ...
  host: { class: 'attributes' },
})
export class SomeComponent {
  @Input('class')
  public klass: string;
}
```

In angular before ng9 for pice of code above we had a bit different behaviour.

In case, when we use our component like `<some-component class="test"></some-component>` for angular 8, after ngOnInit, we had only "test" in "klass" variable. But for angular 9 we have concatenated input property with host.class and now it equals klass === "attributes test" for example above.

It looks strange and logically at the same time. Possibly, there is feature of Ivy, but I want to clarify and be sure that its not a bug of Ivy and ng9.

My examples for reproduction is totally the same with only one thing different - angular version.

## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction
For angular version 8 and early: https://ng-run.com/edit/urRUMm5njGb9EAOsgtuh

For angular version 9: https://ng-run.com/edit/y5YZ2sHv9uC0N900mHAz

## 🔥 Exception or Error
I expect that it works like before. So, @Input('class') doesn't affected with host.class

## 🌍  Your Environment

**Angular Version:**

angular 8.2.14 and angular 9.0
comments:
See for explanation:
https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/389379918303391d07fb5b2a074bf8b00dc66e6b/packages/core/src/render3/instructions/styling.ts#L253-L267

This is expected/intended/correct behavior.

Assume you have your own component `<greet>` with property `name`
```
@Component({
  selector: `greet'
})
class GreetComponent {
  @Input('name')
  name: string;

  @Input('class')
  klass: string;
}
```

Therefore in this example: 
```
<greet name="World"></greet>
<greet [name]="expression"></greet>
```
In the above example both of the cases will assign to `name` property of `<greet>`. Therefore for consistency the following example should behave same.
```
<greet class="World"></greet> // CASE A
<greet [class]="expression"></greet>
```
So the fact that in View Engine case A does not work is a bug with VE as it is inconsistent with the rest of template syntax behavior. 

Finally in the last example
```
<greet class="World" [class]="expression"></greet>
```
one would expect that both values get concatenated before they are written to the property, which is exactly the behavior of Ivy.

Closing as working as intended.
Discussed offline: we are going to discuss this one more internally.
A slightly simpler / cleaned up repro to make it easier to understand: https://ng-run.com/edit/VdKnp2SsVSCHOJPvpuA7?open=app%2Fapp.component.ts

review_comments:
Might want to add the reason why this needs to be stored separately from `tNode.styles`, e.g.

```suggestion
   * (e.g. `<div style="width:200px;">`)
   * Must be stored separately from `tNode.styles` to facilitate setting directive 
   * inputs that shadow the `style` property. 
   * If we used `tNode.styles` as is for shadowed inputs, we would feed host styles 
   * back into directives as "inputs". 
   * If we used `tNode.attrs`, we would have to concatenate the attributes on 
   * every template pass. Instead, we process once on first create pass and store here.
   
```
